edusperience_description: In this 'Mini-Essay' project, you'll write an introduction and body paragraph analyzing whether Odysseus is truly a hero in The Odyssey by Homer. Heroes represent the most valued qualities of a culture, yet concepts of heroism vary greatly across time and societies. By examining Odysseus's actions through Ancient Greek standards and through a modern lens, you'll craft a well-structured argument supported by textual evidence.

objectives.section_description: This is where your writing begins! In this section, you'll write your full draft consisting of two strong paragraphs that analyze whether Odysseus is truly a hero. Each paragraph serves a clear purpose and follows specific academic formatting requirements. Introduction Paragraph: Begin with a hook to grab your reader's attention, mention the epic's title and author, briefly summarize the story, and end with a strong thesis statement that answers whether Odysseus is a hero. Body Paragraph: Focus on evidence from The Odyssey that supports your position. Use two well-chosen quotes from Homer's epic, provide commentary that explains each quote both within the text and in relation to modern heroism, and make sure everything ties back to your thesis. Formatting Requirements: Use 12-point Times New Roman font throughout. Left-align all text and use the tab key to indent the first line of each paragraph. Do not add blank lines between paragraphs—your essay should be continuous from introduction through body paragraph. Proper formatting demonstrates your ability to follow MLA conventions and produce professional academic writing. Aim for 350–500 words total.

objectives.section_description: This is where your writing begins! In this section, you'll write your full draft consisting of two strong paragraphs that analyze whether Odysseus is truly a hero. Each paragraph serves a clear purpose and follows specific academic formatting requirements. Introduction Paragraph: Begin with a hook to grab your reader's attention, mention the epic's title and author, briefly summarize the story, and end with a strong thesis statement that answers whether Odysseus is a hero. Body Paragraph: Focus on evidence from The Odyssey that supports your position. Use two well-chosen quotes from Homer's epic, provide commentary that explains each quote both within the text and in relation to modern heroism, and make sure everything ties back to your thesis. Formatting Requirements: Use 12-point Times New Roman font throughout. Left-align all text and use the tab key to indent the first line of each paragraph. Do not add blank lines between paragraphs—your essay should be continuous from introduction through body paragraph. Proper formatting demonstrates your ability to follow MLA conventions and produce professional academic writing. Aim for 350–500 words total.

objectives.objective_description: Before submitting, review your body paragraph carefully. Start with a clear topic sentence that elaborates on your thesis and provides focus for your argument about Odysseus's heroism. Locate both quotes and confirm each comes directly from The Odyssey wrapped in "double quotation marks"; not paraphrases or summaries. Check that you introduced each quote with context so readers understand where it comes from and why it matters, and verify that both quotes are relevant to heroism and support your thesis. After each quote, include two separate commentaries: the first explaining how the evidence connects to your thesis within The Odyssey, and the second explaining how it connects to real-world heroism or modern applications. Don't just retell what happened; explain why the evidence matters and how it proves your argument. Review your concluding sentences to ensure you restate your thesis using different words (not copying from your introduction), summarize your main evidence and arguments without word-for-word repetition, and explain why your position on Odysseus's heroism matters by addressing the broader significance of your analysis. Your conclusion should reinforce your argument, wrap up key points, and help readers understand why this analysis is important.

objectives.objective_description: Before submitting, check that your essay uses analytical language and flows smoothly. Begin commentary sentences with explanation starters like "This evidence shows that...", "This fact reveals...", "One can see...", or "It is clear that..." to introduce analysis rather than summary; don't just retell what happened in the quotes. Use transition words (for example, similarly, for instance, in addition, furthermore, however, therefore) to connect ideas within and between sections, showing clear relationships between your evidence and commentary so the essay flows without abrupt jumps. Maintain academic writing conventions by avoiding informal language ("you", "your", "things", "stuff", "very", "really") and first-person phrases ("In this essay, I will..." or "I think..."). Keep a formal, objective tone suitable for literary analysis, and capitalize all proper nouns correctly, including Odysseus, Homer, and The Odyssey. Verify your formatting meets MLA requirements: use 12-point Times New Roman font throughout, double-space the entire document with no extra space between paragraphs, center-align your title, indent the first line of both paragraphs, and left-align all other text. Check that spelling, punctuation, and capitalization are correct, sentence structure is varied with proper subject-verb agreement, and your writing is clear and readable.
